scores.interpretation: This is the strongest red signal in the filing and is OUTSIDE the J-Book pattern. A Big-4 auditor declaring ICFR ineffective specifically on revenue recognition — for a company that just realigned segments mid-year, grew revenue 33.5% to $2.78B, and posted operating loss vs prior-year operating income — should be treated as SEVERE. Combined with the prior 10-K/A restatement (May 2025), this is a multi-year accounting-quality issue. While not part of the J-Book divergence cohort, the framework correctly surfaces it. EDGAR FTS lookup returned 0 hits but the disclosure is directly verified in the audited financials.

_summary.cohort_verdict: AXON does not exhibit the J-Book exposure divergence pattern. The filing names no Pentagon Program Element, no PE number, no DoD program-of-record. Total DoD revenue is ~$3.4M against $2.78B total revenue (0.12%). pentagon_jbook fired NOT_FOUND on every J-Book-grounded claim. The strongest negative signal is OUTSIDE this cohort: a PwC-identified ICFR material weakness on revenue recognition (c10), the second consecutive year of accounting issues. The acq_coherence MIXED signal on the Dedrone acquisition (c5/c6) is a secondary integration-risk flag. ITA inclusion in this cohort appears miscalibrated for AXON — it is a commercial public-safety company with negligible DoD exposure.
